clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with a 1-week history of progressive left lower limb weakness, numbness, absent left ankle reflex, and diffuse weakness with diminished sensory modalities distal to mid-calf. Lumbar spine MRI performed 8 days from symptom onset showed bilateral cauda equina nerve root enhancement sparing the lumbosacral plexuses. NCS/EMG demonstrated asymmetric left lower limb plexopathy with absent tibial H-reflex and reduced recruitment in key muscles. CSF analysis 12 days from symptom onset revealed cytoalbuminologic dissociation with normal cell count, without oligoclonal bands. Microbiological and autoimmune blood and CSF testing were negative, and CT scans showed no malignancy. The diagnosis of nondiabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy was made. The patient received IVIg treatment 13–17 days from symptom onset. No further rehabilitation was required. The clinical course, treatment response, and exclusion of diabetic and other systemic causes is consistent with nondiabetic LRPN.
